_comment: Engine registry for bench/run.py. 'launch' engines are started by the harness (one process per model, so peak memory is per model); 'url' engines are attached to where they already run. Template variables: {port} {model_root} {model_dir} {model_id} {memory_ceiling_bytes} {repo}. Binaries resolve from <bin_env> first, then PATH, then the literal path. Platforms: which platform's leaderboard the engine can appear on; iOS rows are produced by in-app harnesses, never by this script.

mlxcat.description: mlxcat native engine over its own HTTP server (mlxcat-http).
mlxcat.notes: Build with: swift build -c release --product mlxcat-http
mlxcat.version: mlxcat-http @ 93dcbc1 (shipping pin; bench/ commits on top do not touch Sources/)

mlxcat-defaults.description: mlxcat with NO memory ceiling — the fair-fight arm. Every competitor on this board runs with MLX's own defaults (memoryLimit 1.5x the recommended working set, cacheLimit equal to it: roughly 54 GiB on a 48 GiB Mac). The `mlxcat` entry passes --memory-ceiling-bytes, which since 7f6cbb6 also clamps the MLX buffer cache to 4 GiB, so the two are not comparable measurements of the same engine. Run both: `mlxcat` is what the product ships, `mlxcat-defaults` is what the comparison is entitled to.
mlxcat-defaults.notes: Same binary as `mlxcat`; the only difference is the absent ceiling, which leaves MemoryGuard.applyAllocatorLimits a no-op and MLX at its defaults. Read the pair as an A/B of what the memory guard costs, never as two engines.
mlxcat-defaults.version: mlxcat-http @ 93dcbc1 (shipping pin; bench/ commits on top do not touch Sources/)

mlxcat-batched.description: mlxcat with the batched-decode serialization exclusions LIFTED for gemma4 and qwen3_5 (MLXCAT_UNSERIALIZE_MODEL_TYPES). NativeModelLoader.usesSerializedDecode switches batched decode off for five of the six leaderboard models, which is why mlxcat's TTFT scales 15-86x from c1 to c8 while every competitor scales 4-9x. Neither exclusion list has been re-earned: the logit-level gate that would justify them was pinned to Qwen3-0.6B-4bit, a model on neither list. Run across families on 2026-08-22, gemma-4-E2B and Qwen3.5-4B both pass under the 1.25 tolerance and under Qwen3-0.6B's own 1.19. This arm measures what lifting them buys.
mlxcat-batched.notes: Same binary and same ceiling as `mlxcat`; the only difference is the env override. Read the pair as an A/B of the exclusion lists, never as two engines.

mlxcat-moe-uncapped.description: mlxcat with the qwen3_moe batching cap REMOVED (MLXCAT_UNSERIALIZE_MODEL_TYPES=qwen3_moe). qwen3_moe used to be `.always` — never batched — on the strength of a throughput claim the repo retired; re-measuring it produced a width rather than a verdict (max logit error 0.94 at batch 2, inside the 1.25 tolerance, and 2.69 at batch 4 and 8, outside it), so the default is now `.maxWidth(2)`. This arm is the same binary with no cap at all. Read the pair `mlxcat` vs `mlxcat-moe-uncapped` as: what does the CAP cost, on top of what serialization cost. The third point — fully serialized — is the pre-ceiling rows measured on the same machine at 78b779f.
mlxcat-moe-uncapped.notes: Same binary and same ceiling as `mlxcat`; the only difference is the env override. Uncapping is NOT a proposal — width 4 and 8 fail the logit tolerance. This arm exists to price the cap, so the cost of the correctness bar is a number rather than an argument.

mlx-swift-lm-tokeniterator.description: mlx-swift-lm's raw TokenIterator loop, in-process — the mlx-swift-examples lineage and EXACTLY the mechanism behind Local AI Cat's legacy LLMEvaluator. The single-sequence baseline mlxcat must not lose to.
mlx-swift-lm-tokeniterator.notes: Build with: swift build -c release --product mlxcat-baseline. transport=in-process; compare to mlxcat-inprocess, not to HTTP rows. Runs under the same allocator policy as the server (--memory-ceiling-bytes), without which a long-context cell drives the host into memory pressure and the row measures swapping rather than the engine.

mlxcat-inprocess.description: MLXCatEngine driven in-process (no HTTP) — the engine's own cost next to the TokenIterator baseline; the HTTP row minus this row is the transport cost.

omlx.description: Stock oMLX (jundot/omlx) — the Python reference mlxcat was ported from.
omlx.notes: NOT on PyPI. Routes: `brew tap jundot/omlx https://github.com/jundot/omlx && brew install omlx` (the repo IS the tap — the URL is required, `brew tap jundot/omlx` alone looks for a nonexistent homebrew-omlx repo), the .dmg app, or from source: `pipx install git+https://github.com/jundot/omlx.git`. Same mlx-community weights; default config. 2026-09-23: installed with `PIPX_HOME=~/.cache/lac-bench/pipx pipx install --python python3.13 'omlx @ git+https://github.com/jundot/omlx.git@v0.6.3rc3'` (Python 3.14 is refused by its <3.14 pin); --base-path isolates its state under ~/.cache/lac-bench/omlx-home. v0.6.4 is newer; the brief pinned rc3.

mlx-lm.description: Apple's mlx-lm reference server (python -m mlx_lm server).
mlx-lm.notes: pipx install mlx-lm (provides the mlx_lm.server binary; `python3 -m mlx_lm` will NOT work from a pipx venv). Single-sequence; no continuous batching.

mlx-serve.description: ddalcu/mlx-serve — Zig core + mlx-c; the other NON-Python native MLX server, and mlxcat's closest architectural rival.
mlx-serve.notes: Two install routes: `brew tap ddalcu/mlx-serve https://github.com/ddalcu/mlx-serve && brew trust ddalcu/mlx-serve && brew install mlx-serve` (brew REFUSES the formula without the trust grant, which is a standing permission to execute that tap's Ruby — prefer the second route on shared machines), or build from source: `git clone` + `brew bundle install --file=Brewfile` (cmake, webp) + `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` → zig-out/bin/mlx-serve, then point MLX_SERVE_BIN at it. Same mlx-community weights via --model-dir. NOTE: mlx-serve defaults to --host 0.0.0.0 (open to the local network); the launch template pins 127.0.0.1 so a benchmark never exposes a model server to the LAN. Prebuilt arm64 binary from its GitHub releases is the least-privilege route (no brew trust, no zig 0.17-dev nightly).

vllm-mlx.description: vllm-mlx (waybarrios) — continuous batching + paged/prefix KV on MLX.
vllm-mlx.notes: pipx install vllm-mlx — installs to ~/.local/bin, which is NOT on a non-interactive zsh PATH; set VLLM_MLX_BIN or add it. Verify the CLI shape against the installed version before trusting a row.

quarantined.reason: Panicked the macOS GPU driver on an M4 Pro mid-suite: panic(cpu 8) "completeMemory() prepare count underflow" @IOGPUMemory.cpp:550, panicked task 'Python', 31 threads. It had just been launched and its first cell (Qwen3.5-4B/short/c1) timed out; the host died ~9 minutes later and took the three queued passes behind it with it. Upstream carries open GPU memory-accounting and stream-ownership defects (waybarrios/vllm-mlx #627, #712, #468) and a closed wired/Metal growth report (#442); no kernel panic is reported there, so treat ours as unreported upstream.

rapid-mlx.description: Rapid-MLX (raullenchai) 0.15.0 — 'Ollama replacement' MLX engine with prompt caching; a fork of vllm-mlx (it installs vllm-mlx binaries alongside its own).
rapid-mlx.notes: pipx install rapid-mlx into ~/.cache/lac-bench. Telemetry (PostHog) is ON by default upstream — the launch passes --no-telemetry AND RAPID_MLX_TELEMETRY=0/DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Lineage risk: vllm-mlx is quarantined here for a GPU-driver panic; run Rapid-MLX last and alone.

swama.description: swama (Trans-N-ai) — native Swift MLX engine; the closest sibling to mlxcat.
swama.notes: Attach-only. Ships a macOS app + CLI; iOS app exists (rows from its app would need its own producer).

swiftlm.description: SwiftLM (SharpAI) — native MLX Swift server, SSD streaming for 100B+ MoE, iOS app support.

lmstudio.notes: lms server start && lms load <model>. Must point LM Studio at the same mlx-community weights (or record the quant it used).
lmstudio.weights: mlx-community 4bit safetensors (LM Studio's own copy of the same repo; verified via `lms ls --json`)
lmstudio.version: LM Studio 0.4.16+2, mlx-llm engine mlx-llm-mac-arm64-apple-metal-nax-advsimd@1.11.0, llama.cpp engine 2.43.0

ollama.description: Ollama — MLX backend by default on Apple Silicon since v0.30 (2026-05); llama.cpp before that.
ollama.weights: ollama library (its own artifacts — NOT the same files; compare with care)
ollama.notes: Port 11434 is Local AI Cat's Local API on our Macs — run Ollama with OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11436 — NOT 11435: the running alpha embeds mlxcat-http on *:11435 (IPv6 wildcard), and an Ollama bound to 127.0.0.1:11435 (IPv4) silently shadows it for every IPv4 loopback client (seen 2026-09-23 01:20-02:05, no alpha traffic reached Ollama). Different weight artifacts; rows are labelled as such. 2026-09-23: Homebrew ollama 0.34.3, OLLAMA_MODELS isolated under ~/.cache/lac-bench/ollama-models; `ollama --version` WITHOUT OLLAMA_HOST reports 'version is 0.5.7' because it is talking to the Cat's :11434 compat endpoint, not to an Ollama server.

llama-cpp.weights: GGUF: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF UD-Q4_K_M (no plain Q4_K_M published there) / unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF Q4_K_M
llama-cpp.notes: Attach-only. Use a Q4_K_M GGUF of the same base model; record it in --tag.

localaicat-legacy.description: Local AI Cat's legacy in-app LLMEvaluator (mlx-swift-lm TokenIterator) through the app's Local API.
localaicat-legacy.notes: Attach to a running Local AI Cat with the engine setting forced to legacy. The alpha on :11434 must NOT be restarted by the harness.

mlxcat-cache-held.description: mlxcat with the MLX buffer-cache releases turned OFF (MLXCAT_IDLE_CLEAR_CACHE=0, MLXCAT_DECODE_CLEAR_CACHE_STEPS=0) — the behaviour that shipped before 2026-08-23. MLX keeps freed Metal buffers on a free list and does not return them, so a process that once served a 16k prompt stayed at that footprint for every later cell; the default now clears on drain-to-idle and every 512 decode steps, which is mlx-lm's interval (guest/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/generate.py:1779). Measured in-process on Qwen3-0.6B with a 4096-token prompt, the difference was 1953 MiB held vs 0. Read the pair `mlxcat` vs `mlxcat-cache-held` as: what does handing the cache back cost in latency, against what it saves in footprint.
mlxcat-cache-held.notes: Same binary and same ceiling as `mlxcat`; the only difference is the two env overrides. This arm is not a proposal — it is the control that makes the default's footprint claim a measurement. Note the peak column is per PROCESS and one process serves every tier of a model, so this arm's later cells inherit its 16k high-water mark; that inheritance IS the defect being priced.

mlxcat-scalar-rope-off.description: mlxcat with the single-row scalar RoPE offset turned OFF (MLXCAT_SINGLE_ROW_SCALAR_ROPE=0) — the behaviour that shipped before 97aa3e5. That commit makes a one-row BatchKVCache report .scalar(p) instead of .batch([p]) so MLX's RoPE fast path stays eligible on single-row decode; reading the scalar costs a host sync, cached per mutation epoch. It landed with its own message saying "Perf A/B queued for the quiet M4" — the A/B was never run, and the next bench pass showed mlxcat's own cold TTFT rising on Qwen3.5-4B (1290->1652 c1, 1951->2940 c2, 3876->5647 c4) with rivals unchanged, which is what turned the parity gate red. Read the pair `mlxcat` vs `mlxcat-scalar-rope-off` as: is the width-1 fast path worth what it costs. NOTE the fast path is gated on batchSize == 1, so it can only explain c1 — if c2/c4 move too, the cause is elsewhere and this arm says so.
mlxcat-scalar-rope-off.notes: Same binary, same ceiling, same everything as `mlxcat`; one env override. This arm is the discriminator the parity-gate regression needs, not a proposal.

mlxcat-admission-clear.description: mlxcat with the admission cache clear ON (MLXCAT_ADMISSION_CLEAR_CACHE=1): MLX's buffer cache is cleared once each time a prefilled row joins the decode batch, so prefill scratch that decode never reuses goes back before the 512-step interval. Idea from ml-explore/mlx-swift-lm#620. Read the pair `mlxcat` vs `mlxcat-admission-clear` as: what does the extra clear cost in TTFT and decode, against what it saves in peak footprint under concurrency. Off by default; see docs/LEVERS.md.

mtplx.description: MTPLX (pip mtplx) — native MTP speculative decoding on MLX. Runs its OWN MTP-bearing checkpoint, not the mlx-community file: a different quant, so a faster row is a caveat, not a win.
mtplx.weights: Youssofal/Qwen3.8-27B-MTPLX-Optimized-Speed @ dea0534a (MTPLX's own MTP checkpoint — different quant from mlx-community 4bit)
mtplx.notes: Attach-only: started by hand with `mtplx serve --model <snapshot> --host 127.0.0.1 --port 12200 --no-auth --yes --no-stats-footer --model-id Qwen3.8-27B-MTPLX-Optimized-Speed` so the served id is stable. Install: PIPX_HOME=~/.cache/lac-bench/pipx pipx install mtplx. --no-stats-footer matters: without it the server appends a stats footer to content.

localai-app-a218.description: The running Local AI Cat alpha a218 on :11434, engine mlxserve (mlxcat embedded) — what Phil's coding sessions actually hit. Attach-only, read-only, single c1 pass.
localai-app-a218.notes: Never change its engine default, never install-latest, never use this port for load. c1 only.

omlx-oq4e-mtp.description: oMLX 0.6.3rc3 serving Jundot's MTP-bearing oQ4e checkpoint (Jundot/Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4e-mtp @ 04dc550) — a DIFFERENT quant (oQ 4-bit, imatrix) from mlx-community 4bit; a faster row is a caveat, not a win.
omlx-oq4e-mtp.notes: omlx serve exposes no MTP flag; whether it engages the checkpoint's MTP head is read from its log, not assumed.
